Task: Open Board Packs list
Standard/framework/pattern gap: gap
Description: Board Packs list view has no usable columns at all - shows only a right-aligned raw 'ID' column (265,266,267,8,7,6,4,3,2); no meeting name, date, status or document reference anywhere in the list.
User impact: A Company Secretary cannot identify which row is which pack without opening every one of the 10 records individually; fails the 5-second test and makes board-pack assembly/distribution unusable from the list.
Governance impact: Undermines audit-readiness of board pack distribution tracking since the record proving which pack went to which meeting cannot be located without opening every record.
Recommendation: Define an explicit <list> view for govoo.board.pack with columns for Meeting, Pack Document, Status and Distribution Date; add a default sort order.
Odoo implementation approach: Add a tree/list view with meaningful fields (related meeting name, state, pack document name, distribution date) instead of the Odoo default fallback list, with a default sort by meeting date.

Task: Open Minutes, Board Pack, and Governance Settings forms
Step: Board & Meetings > Minutes (and Board Packs); Configuration > Governance Settings
Standard/framework/pattern gap: gap
Description: Several record forms show the raw technical model name plus DB id as breadcrumb/tab title instead of a human-readable name, e.g. 'govoo.minutes,4', 'govoo.board.pack,8', 'govoo.governance.config,42' - a pattern across at least three models with no _rec_name/display_name producing readable text.
User impact: Confusing, unprofessional, and makes multi-tab/multi-record navigation unreliable for a non-technical user who cannot tell which meeting's minutes a tab holds.
Governance impact: A board pack or minutes record meant to be audit/board-ready should never surface internal implementation details; visible credibility issue during a director or auditor screen-share.
Recommendation: Add a computed display name (via _compute_display_name or a stored name field) to govoo.minutes, govoo.board.pack and govoo.governance.config so breadcrumbs and tab titles show readable text.
Odoo implementation approach: Ensure each affected model computes a proper display_name/name field (e.g. 'Minutes - Board Meeting - Q4 2026') used by the generic form view breadcrumb.

Task: Review Governance Settings configuration
Standard/framework/pattern gap: gap
Description: Field help tooltips expose raw internal developer/spec annotations verbatim, e.g. '[CONFIRM] BR-BOARD-008 / open-decisions.md item 3...', referencing internal requirement IDs and a spec file that mean nothing to the end user; none of this context is visible on the form itself (only on hover), and the visible value is just '0' with no banner explaining it is an intentionally-unset placeholder.
User impact: A secretary seeing four statutory deadlines at 0 and an unchecked e-signature box (without hovering every '?' icon) would reasonably conclude the system is broken, not that these are deliberately held open pending legal confirmation; could act on the literal '[CONFIRM]' jargon as an instruction meant for them.
Governance impact: If a secretary does not realize these legal-threshold fields are placeholders, they could assume compliance deadline tracking (charge registration, UBO declaration, share certificate/transfer deadlines) is active when effectively disabled (0 days), risking missed statutory deadlines.
Recommendation: Strip internal spec references from user-facing field help text and add an in-form warning banner summarizing which statutory values are still unconfirmed placeholders.
Odoo implementation approach: Render plain-language help strings (e.g. 'Not yet confirmed by legal counsel. Leave at 0 to keep reminders off.') and add a visible on-form banner when any [CONFIRM] field is still at its default, consistent with the existing Minutes 'has not been drafted yet' banner pattern.

Task: Open a Resolution form and review its voting activity/chatter
Step: Board & Meetings > Resolutions > open a resolution (Open for Voting / Passed)
Standard/framework/pattern gap: gap
Description: The 'Vote on resolution' planned activity is assigned to the system account OdooBot rather than the individual director(s) who need to vote; shown 20 days overdue on an Open-for-Voting resolution, and chatter on a Passed resolution shows 'OdooBot: To-Do done' even though three named directors actually cast the votes.
User impact: Breaks the expectation that activities/reminders are personal, assignable tasks tied to a real person.
Governance impact: Board voting accountability and the audit trail of who was asked to vote and when is a core GRC requirement; routing it through a generic bot account instead of named directors undermines the tamper-evident, individually-attributable record the system should provide.
Recommendation: Fix the automated activity-creation logic for resolution voting so each director gets their own vote reminder activity; audit other automations for the same OdooBot-assignment pattern.
Odoo implementation approach: When a resolution moves to 'Open for Voting', create one mail.activity per eligible voter assigned to that director's res.users record, not the public/bot user.

Task: View Dashboard on mobile
Standard/framework/pattern gap: gap
Description: On a 390px mobile viewport the three Dashboard panels render as fixed-width mini tables; only the first column (title) is visible, with Meeting Type, Committee, Start Date, Quorum Met, Status, Result and Effective Date pushed off-screen behind a nested horizontal scrollbar inside each card.
User impact: The single most useful piece of information (status/urgency) is effectively hidden on mobile; the nested horizontal-scroll gesture is easy to miss on a touchscreen since it looks identical to the page's vertical scroll.
Governance impact: Reduces the practical reliability of the mobile dashboard for monitoring overdue compliance items and pending votes outside the office.
Recommendation: Make the dashboard's embedded mini-tables responsive (stacked key/value cards on narrow viewports) instead of relying on nested horizontal scroll.
Odoo implementation approach: Switch the dashboard's embedded list widgets to a responsive card/stacked layout below a breakpoint, similar to how the full Meetings list already reflows into kanban-style cards on mobile.

Task: Open Meetings list and Compliance Instances list, check default filters
Standard/framework/pattern gap: gap
Description: Neither list applies any default filter or group-by even though both have one available ('Upcoming (30 days)' and Status Late/Upcoming/Filed/Waived); all 11 meetings and 10 compliance instances show together, unsorted by urgency, every session.
User impact: Extra clicks and cognitive load for a power user who must manually scan a flat list mixing years-old closed records with urgent upcoming ones, or re-apply the filter every session.
Governance impact: Increases the chance a late compliance obligation or imminent meeting is overlooked because it isn't visually prioritized by default.
Recommendation: Apply a sensible default filter (e.g. 'Upcoming/Late') and default sort order on the Meetings and Compliance Instances list actions.
Odoo implementation approach: Set a default search_default_* context key on the menu action and a default sort order (due date / start date ascending) in the action definition.

Task: Trigger a validation error on a new Meeting
Step: Board & Meetings > Meetings > New > Save with required fields blank
Standard/framework/pattern gap: gap
Description: Required fields (Meeting Name, Meeting Type, Committee, Start Date) show no asterisk/icon in their normal state; only after a failed Save do labels/borders turn red with no accompanying text message anywhere on the page.
User impact: No upfront indication of which fields are mandatory; a colorblind user may not perceive the red highlighting as an error state since no text accompanies it.
Governance impact: Low - mainly an efficiency issue since invalid records cannot actually be saved.
Recommendation: Show a persistent required-field asterisk before save is attempted, and surface a plain-language toast alongside the red highlighting.
Odoo implementation approach: Verify required=True fields render Odoo's standard asterisk styling (view/field definitions may be suppressing it) and ensure the save-error notification includes a text summary, not just field highlighting.

Task: Review Resolutions list for traceability
Standard/framework/pattern gap: gap
Description: The resolution 'Approve Consulting Services Agreement with TechHub Rwanda Ltd' has an empty Meeting column while Status/Result both show 'Passed'; every other resolution in the list links to a named meeting.
User impact: Breaks one-click traceability between related governance records that the rest of the app otherwise supports well.
Governance impact: A resolution without a linked meeting record is a genuine audit-trail gap for a passed board decision.
Recommendation: Require a linked meeting before a resolution can be marked Passed/Failed, and fix this existing orphaned record.
Odoo implementation approach: Make the meeting_id field required (or validated) before a resolution can move out of Draft; backfill/relink the orphaned record.

Task: Open AI Configuration
Standard/framework/pattern gap: gap
Description: Unlike Governance Settings (auto-provisioned, shown '1/1'), AI Configuration opens to Odoo's generic empty 'Create new document' state with no explanatory text about what it controls or why none exists.
User impact: A secretary checking whether AI features are enabled sees an empty screen and cannot tell whether that means AI is off, not yet set up, or broken.
Governance impact: Low direct governance impact, but the org's hard rules require every Enterprise/AI feature to degrade gracefully and be clearly flagged - an unexplained empty config screen doesn't communicate that state.
Recommendation: Auto-provision a default (disabled) AI Configuration record per company, consistent with the Governance Settings pattern, or add explanatory empty-state copy.
Odoo implementation approach: Treat govoo.ai.config as a singleton like govoo.governance.config (auto-create one record per company on module install), or add a guided 'Enable AI' empty-state action.

Task: 5-second test on Dashboard home
Standard/framework/pattern gap: gap
Description: The dashboard panel 'Open Resolutions Requiring My Vote' frames content as a personal voting task; a Company Secretary typically administers/records board votes rather than casting their own.
User impact: Minor terminology mismatch that could cause momentary confusion about role responsibilities.
Governance impact: None directly; a labeling/clarity issue, not a data-access issue.
Recommendation: Use role-neutral or role-aware wording for shared dashboard panels so non-voting roles aren't addressed as if they were voters.
Odoo implementation approach: Rename the panel per-role (e.g. 'Resolutions Open for Voting' for secretarial/admin roles, keeping 'Requiring My Vote' only for director logins) or confirm via role-based dashboard variants.

Task: Open Board & Meetings > Meetings, open a meeting, edit a field, attempt to save
Step: Opened 'Board Meeting - Q1 2027', edited Meeting Name to 'TEST EDIT', clicked Save
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Segregation-of-duties / RBAC expectation for a read-only admin role; ISQM 1 access-control quality management
Description: Expected Access-Denied/read-only behavior for this config/admin-focused role; instead the edit saved with zero access-control error, no warning, no disabled styling. All Meeting fields are plain editable textboxes, the 'New' button works, the statusbar 'Mark as Held' button is enabled, and the companion Resolution form exposes 'Tally Votes'/'Withdraw' (normally Secretary/Chair actions). Chatter correctly logged the change, proving the edit that should never have been possible actually happened.
User impact: A Board Administrator can silently rename meetings, remove attendees, alter agenda items, and progress a meeting's or resolution's workflow state without any warning that this exceeds their intended authority.
Governance impact: Undermines segregation of duties, a core control under ISQM 1 and sound governance practice; a regulator/auditor reviewing RBAC would flag this as a control deficiency since any 'Board Administrator' can alter board minutes, attendee lists and resolution outcomes.
Recommendation: Add a record rule/field-level ir.rule or group-based readonly attrs so govoo.board.meeting (and govoo.board.resolution) fields and workflow buttons are readonly/invisible for the Board Administrator group; hide the 'New' action; add an explicit banner if partial read-only is intended.
Odoo implementation approach: Define/verify a dedicated security group (e.g. govoo_board.group_board_admin) distinct from govoo_board.group_board_secretary; set perm_write=0 in ir.model.access.csv for that group, or use field-level groups attribute + states-based readonly; ensure statusbar buttons use groups="govoo_board.group_board_secretary" so they are invisible, not just blocked.

Task: Open Configuration > Governance Settings
Standard/framework/pattern gap: No raw technical identifiers in user-facing UI (microcopy heuristic)
Description: The record's breadcrumb, header and browser tab title all display the raw technical identifier 'govoo.governance.config,42' instead of a human-readable label such as 'Governance Settings' or the company name - the one Configuration screen this role is meant to actively use.
User impact: A non-technical administrator sees a cryptic model.name,id string as the page title, damaging trust in the software and making the screen harder to identify when switching tabs or using browser history/bookmarks.
Governance impact: Low direct governance risk, but a quality/polish signal relevant to 'fit for purpose system' expectations for board administration tooling.
Recommendation: Implement a name compute or _rec_name/display_name override on govoo.governance.config (e.g. 'Governance Settings - <company name>') bound to the form view's title.
Odoo implementation approach: Add name = fields.Char(compute='_compute_name', store=True) or override display_name on govoo.governance.config and set it as _rec_name.

Task: Open Configuration > Governance Settings
Standard/framework/pattern gap: AGENTS.md hard rule: no hard-coded legal values; compliance threshold validation
Description: All four statutory deadline fields (Charge Registration, Beneficial Owner Declaration, Share Certificate Issuance, Share Transfer Registration) are set to 0 - not a plausible real legal value and indistinguishable from an un-configured default.
User impact: If any compliance-reminder/RAG logic reads these thresholds, a 0-day deadline makes every related obligation appear instantly overdue or silently skips the calculation, producing false alarms or missed real deadlines.
Governance impact: Direct conflict with the project's own 'No hard-coded legal values' hard rule, and a genuine compliance risk since these are legally mandated time limits under Rwandan company law.
Recommendation: Add an @api.constrains rejecting 0/negative values for these Integer fields (or requiring explicit confirmation); ship the real default via a data XML record flagged [CONFIRM] rather than a Python literal; show a persistent warning banner when any statutory deadline is 0.
Odoo implementation approach: Seed fields from a data file with active=False sample values and a [CONFIRM] comment per repo convention; block the page from presenting 0 as a valid saved value until a real figure is entered.

Task: Open Statutory Registers > Register of Charges
Step: Navigated to Statutory Registers > Register of Charges
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Statutory register completeness/accuracy (Companies Act / RERA); ISA audit-evidence sufficiency
Description: The Register of Charges contains a record named '[LIVE-TEST #236] Reminder Fixture Partner' (RWF 5,000,000, Satisfied) sitting alongside two genuine Bank of Kigali Plc charges - an unmistakable developer/QA test fixture referencing GitHub issue #236 leaked into production-looking statutory data.
User impact: A Board Administrator (or external auditor/regulator) sees a fabricated charge mixed into the real register with no visual distinction, damaging confidence in the register's accuracy and completeness.
Governance impact: A Register of Charges with fabricated entries is a direct compliance and audit-evidence integrity issue under Companies Law statutory register requirements and ISA standards; would constitute a misstatement if it reached a real filing or external audit review.
Recommendation: Immediately purge/archive all '[LIVE-TEST #...]'/fixture records from any register, cap table, or statutory list reachable in the demo/staging environment; add a CI check that fails module install/tests if a register record's name matches a test-fixture naming pattern.
Odoo implementation approach: Review how govoo_rw.email reminder tests/fixtures create govoo.register.charge records; ensure test-only data uses a disposable test database/transaction rollback (Odoo TransactionCase) rather than writing into the demo/seed company's live register.

Task: Open Statutory Registers > Audit Ledger
Step: Navigated to Statutory Registers > Audit Ledger
Standard/framework/pattern gap: No raw technical identifiers in a statutory audit-trail screen
Description: Every one of 26 rows in the 'Register' column displays the raw technical model name (govoo.register.charge, govoo.register.member, govoo.register.director, govoo.register.beneficial.owner) instead of a human-readable label like 'Register of Charges'.
User impact: A Board Administrator reviewing the audit ledger cannot tell which register was affected without technical Odoo knowledge, defeating the purpose of exposing this ledger to a non-developer role.
Governance impact: Reduces the practical usability of the statutory audit trail for board oversight and external audit review; an auditor sampling this ledger would need to separately map technical names to legal register names.
Recommendation: Map the technical model name to its human label before rendering the Audit Ledger list/form.
Odoo implementation approach: Add a computed Char field, e.g. register_label = fields.Char(compute='_compute_register_label'), looking up ir.model.name for the stored technical model, used instead of the raw register_model field in the tree/list view.

Task: Open Statutory Registers > Audit Ledger
Step: Reviewed the 'Changed By' column across all 26 audit ledger entries
Standard/framework/pattern gap: ISA 230 audit documentation - responsible-party attribution; AGENTS.md audit-trail hard rule
Description: Every single entry in the 'Changed By' column reads 'OdooBot', spanning Mar 2015 through Oct 2026 across director, member, charge and beneficial-owner registers; no real user (Aline Mukamana, Eric Mugisha, Administrator - all seen elsewhere in the system) is ever attributed as the author of a statutory register change.
User impact: The audit ledger - whose entire purpose is accountability - cannot answer 'who did what and when'; it attributes 100% of historical statutory register changes to a system bot account rather than the responsible officer.
Governance impact: Direct audit-trail integrity defect; ISA 230 and governance good practice require statutory records to show the actual responsible party for a change - any auditor testing register completeness/accuracy would flag this.
Recommendation: Ensure audit ledger entry creation captures self.env.user (the user who triggered the register change) rather than defaulting to the data-seeding/automation user; distinguish seed/demo-data entries from genuine user-triggered changes.
Odoo implementation approach: In the create/write override (or logging method) populating govoo.audit.ledger, replace the hardcoded/default author with self.env.user.id; verify this isn't being overwritten by noupdate data-file seeding using the system/OdooBot context during module install.

Task: Assess home screen and resolution record for role-appropriateness
Step: Reviewed Dashboard 'Open Resolutions Requiring My Vote' widget and the resolution form's action buttons
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Role-based home dashboard should not misrepresent a user's authority
Description: The Dashboard addresses the Board Administrator directly with 'Open Resolutions Requiring My Vote' and the resolution record exposes 'Tally Votes'/'Withdraw' actions to the same account, yet this role should be read-only on resolutions; there is no actual voting widget on the resolution form itself (empty Votes tab, no Cast Vote control), so the dashboard framing is inconsistent with what the role can/should do.
User impact: Confusing mixed signal: the dashboard implies a personal vote pending while the resolution record offers governance-level tally/withdraw actions instead; a real administrator would not know whether to vote, administer voting, or neither.
Governance impact: Role-based home screens that misrepresent a user's authority increase the risk of inappropriate actions being taken on resolutions that determine real corporate decisions.
Recommendation: Scope dashboard widgets by security group so 'Open Resolutions Requiring My Vote' only appears for actual resolution voters; show Board Administrators a differently-labeled, non-actionable list instead.
Odoo implementation approach: Add a groups domain or dynamic qweb condition on the dashboard widget definition keyed off the viewing user's security group membership, rather than one shared layout for all governance roles.

Task: Review activity/chatter on an open resolution
Step: Opened 'Approve Revised Risk Management Policy' resolution and reviewed Planned Activities
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Activities should be assigned to accountable human users
Description: The Planned Activities panel shows '20 days overdue: Vote on resolution... for OdooBot' - a scheduled voting reminder assigned to the system bot account rather than a real board member.
User impact: A Board Administrator reviewing this record sees an overdue task assigned to a non-human account, confusing and signaling the activity/reminder automation is misconfigured for this resolution's voter assignment.
Governance impact: Overdue, bot-assigned voting activities undermine confidence in the meeting/voting reminder system the organization's own recent work (wiring real email reminders) is meant to deliver reliably.
Recommendation: Ensure vote-reminder mail.activity records are created with user_id set to the actual board member/voter, not the technical user that ran the seeding/automation script; skip activity creation for non-human users.
Odoo implementation approach: Audit the cron/automation that schedules 'Vote on resolution' activities (likely in govoo_board) to confirm it resolves user_id from the resolution's actual voter list rather than defaulting to self.env.user during demo-data loading.

Task: Open AI > Request Log
Step: Reviewed the AI Requests list columns
Standard/framework/pattern gap: No raw internal ticket codes/vendor strings in user-facing UI
Description: The 'Feature' column shows internal feature codes verbatim ('AI-F07: Data Extraction', 'AI-F08: Semantic Search (RAG)', 'AI-F09: Governance Q&A') and 'Model Used' shows a raw provider:model string ('openai:gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18') rather than a friendly label.
User impact: Minor - a non-technical administrator sees internal feature ticket codes and vendor/model identifiers with no business meaning.
Governance impact: Negligible governance impact; purely a polish/microcopy issue.
Recommendation: Strip the 'AI-F0x:' prefix in the UI label (keep it internally for traceability); show a friendly model name (e.g. 'GPT-4o mini') with the raw string available on hover/tooltip.
Odoo implementation approach: Add a selection field or computed display label for feature on the AI request log model instead of storing/displaying the ticket-style code directly; add a small provider/model name-mapping dict.

Task: Review default filters on Board & Meetings > Meetings and Resolutions lists
Step: Opened Meetings and Resolutions list views
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Default filter/favourite expectation for power-user efficiency
Description: Neither the Meetings list (11 records) nor the Resolutions list (11 records) has any default filter or visible saved favourite applied on load; both show the full unfiltered historical set.
User impact: For a power/admin user working across many historical meetings and resolutions, manually filtering every time to find current/actionable items adds friction, though the small dataset (11 rows) does not yet make it painful.
Governance impact: Low - primarily an efficiency concern rather than a compliance one.
Recommendation: Ship a default/favourite filter such as 'Upcoming & Draft' for Meetings and 'Open for Voting' for Resolutions so first load already surfaces actionable records.
Odoo implementation approach: Add a context with search_default_<filter> on the ir.actions.act_window records for these menu items, backed by a <filter> in the search view already defined (or newly added).

Task: View meeting details as a director restricted to the Board of Directors committee
Step: /my/meetings and /my/meetings/<id> for Audit Committee / Risk & Compliance Committee meetings
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Committee-level confidentiality control gap vs. governance structure design
Description: Grace Uwimana is appointed only to the 'Board of Directors' committee, yet /my/meetings lists and lets her open full detail pages for Audit Committee and Risk & Compliance Committee meetings, showing committee name, date, status, location, agenda and board-pack status for committees she does not sit on. No confidentiality cue or filtering by committee membership is applied anywhere.
User impact: A director can read governance information - and once distributed, full board packs with financials and resolutions - belonging to a committee they are not a member of.
Governance impact: Breaks committee-level confidentiality controls expected for audit/risk committees; could expose commercially or legally sensitive committee deliberations to directors outside that committee - a finding in any external governance or security review.
Recommendation: Filter /my/meetings (and block direct /my/meetings/<id> access) to only meetings of committees the logged-in partner is an active member of; return the same access-denied page used for out-of-scope ids when a non-member director requests a meeting.
Odoo implementation approach: In the portal controller for meeting routes, add a domain/check against the committee membership model (govoo.board.membership) for request.env.user.partner_id before rendering MeetingDetail/MeetingList; add a regression test asserting a non-member director gets 403/redirect.

Task: Cast a vote on a board resolution via the portal
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Explicit confirmation expected for a once-only, binding action
Description: After clicking 'Submit Vote' the browser silently redirects to /my/votes with no success banner, toast, or explicit confirmation text; the only feedback is that the voted item disappears from the list. Reproduced identically on desktop and mobile.
User impact: A director casting a vote on a potentially high-stakes special resolution has no explicit assurance the vote was recorded.
Governance impact: For an audit-grade voting trail, absence of an explicit confirmation step undermines director confidence and could lead to disputes over whether a vote was actually cast.
Recommendation: Show an explicit confirmation message/page after vote submission (e.g. 'Your vote (For) on ... was recorded at <timestamp>') as its own screen rather than a bare redirect; consider emailing a vote receipt as already done for other reminders.
Odoo implementation approach: In the portal controller handling the vote POST, set an ir.qweb flash/notification parameter or render a dedicated confirmation template before redirecting; reuse the existing mail template infrastructure to also send a vote receipt.

Task: Understand what is being voted on before casting a vote
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Informed-consent/voting standard - full resolution text must be accessible before a vote
Description: The vote-cast page shows only a short title, resolution type and committee - no resolution text/body, no link to the meeting, no link to the board pack. Conversely the meeting detail page's agenda has no link to the corresponding vote on /my/votes. The two records are not cross-linked in either direction.
User impact: A director is asked to vote For/Against/Abstain on a resolution title alone, with no way to review the full wording or supporting rationale, and no path to find which meeting/agenda item the vote relates to.
Governance impact: Voting without visible access to the full resolution text and board-pack context undermines informed decision-making, a core requirement of sound board governance.
Recommendation: Add the full resolution text (or rendered HTML body) to the vote-cast page plus a breadcrumb/link back to the originating meeting and board pack; add a corresponding 'Vote open' badge/link on the meeting detail agenda row.
Odoo implementation approach: Extend the govoo.board.resolution portal template to include resolution_text and a computed link to meeting_id; add a smart-button-equivalent link in the QWeb agenda table when an agenda line maps to an open resolution.

Task: Navigate directly to a meeting record the director should not see
Step: Requested /my/meetings/12 and /my/meetings/1 (ids not belonging to this director, no access_token)
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Access-denied states should be explicit, not silent (security UX good practice)
Description: Requesting an out-of-scope meeting id silently redirects to /my (portal home) with absolutely no message - indistinguishable from a broken link.
User impact: A director who clicks a stale/incorrect link gets no explanation and may assume the application is broken rather than understanding it is a deliberate access restriction.
Governance impact: Low direct governance risk since the behavior is fail-safe (denies access), but the lack of a clear message is a poor security UX pattern that could mask genuine bugs from users and QA.
Recommendation: Show a plain-language 'This meeting is not available to you' (or standard Odoo portal 403) page rather than a silent redirect to the unrelated home page.
Odoo implementation approach: In the meeting portal controller's except clause for AccessError/MissingError, render the standard portal 403/404 template (http.request.not_found() or the Odoo portal security page) instead of a bare redirect('/my').

Task: Find the meeting that needs attention among many meetings
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Guided minimal view for occasional users (C8)
Description: /my/meetings lists 11 meetings (2026-2027, mixed statuses and committees) as one flat, unfiltered, unsorted-by-relevance list with no search box, status filter, 'upcoming only' default, or grouping by committee/date; only differentiation is a small colored status pill.
User impact: A director with many historical meetings must visually scan the whole list to find the next upcoming meeting or distinguish it from closed ones; no default view optimized for 'what's next'.
Governance impact: For an occasional user, the lack of a guided minimal view increases the chance of missing an upcoming meeting that needs preparation.
Recommendation: Default to showing only upcoming/scheduled meetings (or group 'Upcoming' vs 'Past' with upcoming expanded first) and add a simple status filter.
Odoo implementation approach: Add a QWeb section split by meeting_date >= today in the portal controller's search/domain logic, mirroring the 'my activities' grouping pattern already used elsewhere in Odoo portal views.

Task: Cast a vote on a phone
Standard/framework/pattern gap: WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8 Target Size, Minimum (24x24 CSS px)
Description: The native radio/checkbox inputs for For/Against/Abstain and the conflict-of-interest declaration measure only 16x16 CSS px, with clickable label rows only 24px tall (326x24) - below the recommended minimum, with the three options stacked immediately adjacent to one another.
User impact: On a 390px phone (this role's expected primary voting device), small closely-packed tap targets increase the risk of mis-tapping 'Against' when intending 'For' on a binding board resolution.
Governance impact: A mis-cast vote on a special resolution due to a UI tap error is a real (if rare) governance risk given how consequential board votes are.
Recommendation: Increase the clickable row height/padding for each radio/checkbox option to at least 44x44 px and add visible spacing between the three vote options.
Odoo implementation approach: Add Bootstrap form-check padding/margin utility classes (e.g. py-2 with min-height) to the vote_choice radio wrapper in the portal QWeb template; no backend change needed.

Task: Choose the correct account at login
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Credential pre-fill is a security-UX anti-pattern
Description: The /web/login 'Choose a user' account switcher pre-fills email AND password fields with the previously-used demo account's credentials (another director's email/password), requiring manual clearing before logging in as the correct director.
User impact: In a shared-browser/demo environment, a user could accidentally submit another account's stored credentials, or be confused about which account they are about to log into; passwords for other demo users are visible in plaintext by default.
Governance impact: Low in production (real directors use individual browsers/sessions), but notable since it reveals login session/credential caching in this instance is broader than expected.
Recommendation: For production, disable the multi-account 'remembered credentials' switcher behavior or at minimum do not pre-fill the password field for a non-active-session account.
Odoo implementation approach: This is core Odoo /web/login behavior (browser autofill + Odoo's account switcher cookie), not a govoo_* customization; flag to IT/ops for session/cookie policy review rather than a module code change.

Task: Cast a vote on an open shareholder resolution
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Weighted-voting transparency at point of decision (good-governance UX standard)
Description: The Cast Vote screen shows only the resolution title, a For/Against/Abstain radio group, a conflict-of-interest checkbox, and Submit/Cancel - it never displays the shareholder's own voting power/weight (e.g. '30,000 votes / 39.47% of voting rights') before submission, even though the Holdings page confirms votes are weighted by share quantity.
User impact: Shareholders cannot verify their voting weight is correctly applied before an irreversible action, undermining confidence in a weighted-voting mechanism core to the product.
Governance impact: Weighted voting is a material governance control; lack of weight disclosure at the point of casting a vote is a transparency gap that could be challenged if a vote outcome is disputed.
Recommendation: Add a visible line on the cast-vote form, e.g. 'You are voting with 30,000 shares (39.47% of Ordinary Shares, weighted voting power 30,000.0)', sourced from the same record used on /my/holdings.
Odoo implementation approach: In the portal controller/QWeb template for the vote-cast route, pass the shareholder's govoo.share.allotment-derived voting power (already computed for /my/holdings) into the render context and display it above the vote radio inputs.

Task: Confirm a vote was recorded after submission
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Feedback/audit-trail UX standard for governance-consequential actions
Description: After clicking 'Submit Vote', the page redirects to /my/holdings/votes with no success message or confirmation of what was recorded; the list then simply reads 'No shareholder resolutions requiring your vote' with no section showing the shareholder's past votes or choice.
User impact: A shareholder cannot tell whether their vote went through, nor can they later confirm their own voting record, which is especially risky for a conflict-of-interest declaration or contested resolution.
Governance impact: Breaks the chain of shareholder-visible accountability/audit trail for voting, a core GRC requirement, even though the vote is presumably logged server-side.
Recommendation: Show a success banner/flash message immediately after submission; add a 'My Vote History' section to /my/holdings/votes listing closed resolutions with the shareholder's own recorded choice and timestamp.
Odoo implementation approach: Use Odoo's portal flash-message pattern (session or QWeb t-if on a query-string flag) for a confirmation banner post-redirect; extend the votes controller/template to also query and render the shareholder's own vote records for closed resolutions.

Task: Understand what needs the shareholder's attention on login
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Role-based home should surface pending approvals/votes, not just static navigation links
Description: At the time of audit one shareholder resolution was open and awaiting this shareholder's vote; the /my landing page nonetheless showed only a static 'Quick Links' list with no count, badge, or callout indicating a vote was pending.
User impact: An occasional-user shareholder could easily miss a vote deadline since nothing on first login flags it.
Governance impact: Risks under-quorum or late voting on resolutions if shareholders are not proactively alerted, which can affect the validity of shareholder decisions.
Recommendation: Add an 'Action needed' card on the portal home summarizing open resolutions awaiting the shareholder's vote (with a deadline, if present) and a direct 'Vote now' call to action.
Odoo implementation approach: In the portal home controller, query open resolution/vote records scoped to the logged-in partner (same query used for /my/holdings/votes) and render a count/callout card above or alongside the Quick Links block.

Task: Make an informed voting decision
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Board/shareholder-pack norms - resolution rationale, proposer and deadline should accompany a vote request
Description: The cast-vote page repeats only the resolution title and a 'Type: ordinary' label; there is no resolution text/rationale, no link to supporting documents, no voting deadline/closing date, and no indication of the majority threshold required.
User impact: Shareholders must vote on a policy change without being shown what the policy actually says, or by when they must decide.
Governance impact: Undermines informed shareholder consent, a core principle of corporate governance; leaves no record of what the shareholder approved beyond a title string.
Recommendation: Display the resolution's full description/body text, any attached documents, the voting deadline, and the pass threshold on both the list and the cast-vote page.
Odoo implementation approach: Extend the govoo.resolution model's existing description/attachment fields (already present for the board-facing view) into the portal QWeb templates for the votes list and cast-vote form.

Task: Understand share class, quantity, percentage ownership and voting power
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Plain-language/microcopy standard - no raw ORM float output to external users
Description: The Holdings page has no on-page heading; the 'Voting Power' column shows unformatted '30000.0' (duplicating Quantity with no explanation of derivation), and there is no total-shares-outstanding figure to contextualize the 39.47% ownership percentage.
User impact: A non-technical shareholder is likely confused why 'Voting Power' repeats 'Quantity' with an odd decimal, and cannot sanity-check the percentage without knowing total shares outstanding.
Governance impact: Low direct governance risk, but erodes trust in the data's polish/accuracy for an externally-facing statutory-adjacent record.
Recommendation: Add a page heading ('My Shareholding'), format Voting Power as an integer or with a tooltip explaining the weighting formula, and show total shares outstanding alongside the percentage.
Odoo implementation approach: Round/format the voting_power field in the QWeb template (e.g. int() cast or format_decimalized_number), add an <h3> page title, and include company-wide total shares in the render context.

Task: Navigate the vote form with a screen reader or keyboard
Standard/framework/pattern gap: WCAG 2.2 AA 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (fieldset/legend grouping)
Description: The 'Your Vote:' label is a plain bold text node, not a <fieldset><legend> wrapping the For/Against/Abstain radio buttons; a screen-reader user tabbing into the group hears only 'For', 'Against', 'Abstain' without reliable grouping context.
User impact: Screen-reader users may not understand what the three radio options represent without also having read preceding visual text.
Governance impact: N/A directly, but accessibility compliance is itself a governance/compliance consideration for a public-facing portal.
Recommendation: Wrap the radio group in a <fieldset><legend>Your Vote</legend> structure.
Odoo implementation approach: Minor QWeb template edit to the vote-cast form partial.

Task: Move between related shareholder records
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Standard Odoo portal sibling-navigation pattern
Description: My Holdings, My Votes, and My Register each show only a single 'Home' breadcrumb icon (no text label) and no way to jump directly to the other two sibling sections without returning to /my first.
User impact: Adds an extra click/round-trip for a shareholder comparing their holdings against an open vote or the full register.
Governance impact: Minor efficiency/traceability friction only.
Recommendation: Add a small persistent sub-nav (My Holdings | My Votes | My Register) at the top of each of these three pages, and give the Home breadcrumb icon a visible text label.
Odoo implementation approach: Add a shared QWeb template snippet included by all three portal templates.

Task: Open a Board Meeting, a Compliance Instance, and a Resolution as the read-only Auditor and check whether workflow/header action buttons are disabled
Standard/framework/pattern gap: ISA-aligned access control expectation; IPPF internal-control principle that UI should reflect actual authority
Description: Across at least three models, statusbar and header action buttons render fully enabled (not greyed out, pointer-events:auto) for the read-only Auditor group, while chatter composer buttons and form fields correctly render disabled/readonly. Concretely: Board Meeting shows active 'Mark as Minuted'/'Close Meeting'; Compliance Instance (Late) shows active 'Record Filing', 'Waive', 'Generate Filing Pack'; Resolution (Open for Voting) shows active 'Tally Votes' and 'Withdraw'. DB verification confirms perm_write=False for the Auditor group on all three models, so a write would likely be rejected server-side, but the buttons themselves are not hidden/disabled the way other elements are.
User impact: Confusing and potentially alarming: a non-technical auditor clicking 'Waive' on a late filing, or 'Tally Votes' on an open resolution, has no visual cue it will fail, and if it fails will see a raw Odoo access-denied error rather than a clear explanation.
Governance impact: An auditor could reasonably believe they are authorized to (and may attempt to) mark minutes finalized, waive a late statutory filing, or tally/withdraw a vote - actions that would directly corrupt the audit trail and statutory record the firm relies on for assurance work.
Recommendation: Add groups="governance_group_write_or_higher" (or an equivalent readonly/invisible domain keyed off a computed is_readonly_role field) to every statusbar/header button across all modules, mirroring the pattern already correctly applied to mail composer buttons and field-level readonly rendering.
Odoo implementation approach: Add an automated UI test that logs in as each read-only role and asserts zero enabled write-triggering buttons are present on every form view.

Task: Open the chatter on a Board Meeting (multiple status transitions) and a Minuted AGM record and assess whether an auditor can reconstruct who-did-what-when
Standard/framework/pattern gap: AGENTS.md hard rule: audit trail / tracking=True on statutory fields; ISA audit-evidence traceability
Description: On every record checked (a meeting that passed Draft > Scheduled > Held; an AGM that passed through 5 statuses to Minuted; a Late compliance instance), the chatter shows only a single system entry '<Model> created' by OdooBot at initial data-load time - no subsequent status transition, field change, or user action appears logged, despite tracking=True being an explicit project requirement for statutory fields.
User impact: An auditor trying to verify governance process integrity (e.g. 'did the Company Secretary, not a Director, record the minutes?') finds nothing in the chatter to answer that question.
Governance impact: Without a change log, an external auditor cannot independently verify who moved a meeting from Held to Minuted, who filed/waived a compliance obligation, or who tallied a vote - a core control gap for segregation-of-duties and non-repudiation testing.
Recommendation: Verify tracking=True is actually set on the state/status field and other statutory fields on govoo.meeting, govoo.minutes, govoo.resolution and govoo.compliance.instance, and that status-transition methods call message_post()/rely on automatic tracking rather than bypassing it.
Odoo implementation approach: Check status-transition methods are not using sudo().write() without tracking context, or raw SQL writes that bypass mail.thread tracking.

Task: Open a Minutes record via the 'Minutes' smart button on an AGM meeting
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Nielsen Norman microcopy heuristic - no raw technical identifiers in user-facing UI
Description: The Minutes form has no display_name/name_get driven title configured, so Odoo falls back to '<model>,<id>' ('govoo.minutes,3') in both the breadcrumb and page heading.
User impact: An auditor sees a cryptic title like 'govoo.minutes,3' instead of 'Minutes - Annual General Meeting 2026', which looks unfinished/unprofessional and briefly confuses non-technical users.
Governance impact: Minor - does not affect governance control, but undermines the 'board/audit-ready' polish expected of statutory record screens.
Recommendation: Implement _compute_display_name (or a name related field) on govoo.minutes composed from the related meeting name, e.g. 'Minutes - Annual General Meeting 2026'.
Odoo implementation approach: Add a stored/computed name field and set _rec_name on govoo.minutes.

Task: List every top-level menu and submenu visible to this role
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Odoo UX convention - a top-level menu with no accessible children should be hidden, not rendered as a dead end
Description: Clicking 'Contract Management' or 'Evaluations' in the top nav visibly highlights the item as active/expanded but opens no dropdown and navigates nowhere; confirmed via DOM query that these menus produce zero submenu items for this role, unlike Statutory Registers, Shares & Cap Table, Board & Meetings and Compliance which correctly populate dropdowns.
User impact: No message, tooltip, or disabled styling explains why the menu is non-functional.
Governance impact: Not a governance-control issue, but a security-UX issue: the auditor cannot tell whether these are empty because the role lacks access (expected) or a configuration bug (unexpected).
Recommendation: Hide top-level menu entries entirely when the resolved role has no visible child menu items.
Odoo implementation approach: Set groups= on the parent <menuitem> to match its children, or compute visibility server-side, instead of leaving an interactive-looking but functionless menu button.

Task: Assess the home screen 5-second test for a read-only role
Standard/framework/pattern gap: GRC UX expectation - landing page should surface 'what needs my attention' and communicate the user's authority level
Description: The Dashboard is not role-specific: Auditor (and presumably every other backend role) sees identical widgets (Upcoming Meetings, Open Resolutions Requiring My Vote, Compliance RAG Summary) with no role-aware relabeling, filtering, or banner, and no indication this is a restricted/read-only session.
User impact: The 'Open Resolutions Requiring My Vote' heading literally tells the auditor they have votes pending, which is false, since the Auditor group has no voting rights.
Governance impact: A read-only external/internal auditor is shown a 'vote' call-to-action identical to a voting Director's, which could create confusion about actual authority during an engagement, and does not direct the auditor toward audit-relevant triage.
Recommendation: Suppress the 'Open Resolutions Requiring My Vote' widget for roles with no voting rights (replace with a neutral 'Resolutions Open for Voting' read-only list), or add a persistent role indicator (e.g. a header badge 'Read-only / Audit view').
Odoo implementation approach: Scope dashboard widgets by security group, mirroring the recommended fix for BOA-007/SEC-010.

Task: Open the chatter/activity panel on an open resolution
Standard/framework/pattern gap: Reminder/escalation automation should target real accountable users
Description: On the 'Approve Revised Risk Management Policy' resolution (Open for Voting), the Activities panel shows a single planned activity assigned to OdooBot, 20 days overdue, rather than to any of the actual voting directors shown in the Votes tab.
User impact: Not a direct auditor-facing harm, but visible evidence (from the auditor's read-only vantage point) of a possibly broken automation.
Governance impact: If voting-reminder activities are scheduled against the system/bot account instead of the actual director, the recently-implemented email reminder feature is not actually notifying anyone responsible for casting the vote, undermining the resolution-tracking control.
Recommendation: Audit the automated activity-scheduling logic for resolution voting reminders to confirm activity_user_id is set to the actual board member/director, not a fallback system user.
Odoo implementation approach: Add a regression test asserting scheduled activities are never assigned to OdooBot/admin in production-like data.
